rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun’s object return is omitted, a common deletion of accusative pronouns in relative clauses; the implied form is “which you kindle.”
rows.anchor: وحذف العائد على الموصول لأن ضمير النصب يكثر حذفه من الصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Kindle the fire” elliptically means kindle its tree, as the following verse makes clear; Arabic commonly omits this genitive complement.
rows.anchor: وتعدية { تورون } إلى ضمير { النار } تعدية على تقدير مضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about creating the fire explains the question “Have you seen the fire,” as the earlier question about creation explained its counterpart.
rows.anchor: وجملة { أأنتم أنشأتم شجرتها } الخ بيان لجملة { أفرأيتم النار } الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence about creating the fire is an appositional specification of “or are We the creators?”
rows.anchor: الجملة بدل اشتمال من جملة { أم نحن المنشئون } ( الواقعة : 72 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating fire serves several purposes, including reminding people of Hell and letting them compare its burning with the harsher fire they know awaits them.
rows.anchor: أن تكون تذكرة للناس يذكرون بها نار جهنم ويوازنون بين إحراقها وإحراق جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matāʿ means something enjoyed or used for a time; Ibn ʿĀshūr points to the phrase “the enjoyment of this world is little” in al-Nisāʾ.
rows.anchor: والمتاع : ما يتمتع ، أي ينتفع به زمانا ، وتقدم في قوله : { قل متاع الدنيا قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muqwī can mean someone in a barren desert, and also a hungry person whose stomach is empty; both senses derive from emptiness.
rows.anchor: والمقوي : الداخل في القواء ( بفتح القاف والمد ) وهي القفر ، ويطلق المقوي على الجائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fire benefits travelers by lighting and warming camps, guiding night travelers to shelter, and enabling people to cook while hungry, at home or on journeys.
rows.anchor: فإن النار متاع للمسافرين يستضيئون بها في مناخهم ويصطلون بها في البرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word gathers both desert traveler and hungry-person senses, folding a reminder of divine favor into the argument; these groups need fire especially.
rows.anchor: فإيثار هذا الوصف في هذه الآية ليجمع المعنيين فإن النار متاع للمسافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the proofs of divine power, resurrection examples, and embedded blessings, God directs the Messenger to a distinctive glorification as a fresh recollection of divine majesty and gratitude.
rows.anchor: رتب على ما مضى من الكلام المشتمل على دلائل عظمة القدرة الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even though the Messenger continually glorifies God, renewed reflection gives each state of worship distinct merits and greater reward.
rows.anchor: فالرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يخلو عن تسبيح ربه والتفكر في عظمة شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The day” may modify an implied predicate of the unbelievers’ humiliating punishment, modify “humiliating,” or be an object of an implied “remember.”
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون { يوم } ظرفا متعلقا بالكون المقدر في خبر المبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating “the day” as an object of an implied “remember” is a familiar Qurʾānic construction; Ibn ʿĀshūr compares 2:30.
rows.anchor: وهذا كثير في أسماء الزمان التي وقعت في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural pronouns refer to those who oppose God and His Messenger and the opponents mentioned before them.
rows.anchor: وضمير الجمع عائد إلى الذين يحادون الله ورسوله } و { الذين من قبلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “All together” is a circumstantial accusative describing the plural pronoun.
rows.anchor: ولذلك أتى بلفظ الشمول وهو { جميعا } حالا من الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their being informed of their deeds threatens exposure of their hypocrisy at resurrection and serves as a euphemism for requital.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { فينبئهم بما عملوا } تهديد بفضح نفاقهم يوم البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God recorded it and they forgot it” is a circumstantial clause attached to “what they did”; its point lies especially in their forgetting.
rows.anchor: وجملة { أحصاه الله ونسوه } في موضع الحال من ( ما عملوا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has known their deeds in full detail all along, while they forgot them in life, exposing their heedlessness and delusion; they will be astonished when confronted with the record.
rows.anchor: أي علمه الله علما مفصلا من الآن ، وهم نسوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene recalls the criminals finding every small and great deed recorded and present in the Book, as described in al-Kahf 18:49.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى : { ووضع الكتاب فترى المجرمين مشفقين مما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing statement is a summation; “witness” here means knowing the matters that are observed.
rows.anchor: وجملة { والله على كل شيء شهيد } تذييل . والشهيد : العالم بالأمور المشاهدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrites whispered together to project unity and frighten Muslims, who feared the talks signaled enemy movement or military defeat; the verses warn that God knows their plotting and informs His Messenger.
rows.anchor: فنزلت هذه الآيات لإشعار المنافقين بعلم الله بماذا يتناجون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah presents the Qurʾān’s greatness and its power to humble its adherents, and closes with divine attributes and universal glorification that commend believers and allude reproachfully to disbelievers.
rows.anchor: وبيان عظمة القرآن وجلالته واقتضائه خشوع أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its discussion also signals the wisdom of Islamic rules for transferring wealth among Muslims without burdening its owners and urges obedience to what God legislates through His Messenger.
rows.anchor: وتخلل ذلك إيماء إلى حكمة شرائع انتقال الأموال بين المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah’s closing declaration that all in heaven and earth glorify God praises believers and implicitly reproaches disbelievers.
rows.anchor: وختمت بصفات عظيمة من الصفات الإلاهية وأنه { يسبح له ما في السماوات والأرض }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening calls believers to glorify God in gratitude for the conquest of Banū al-Naḍīr, as though telling them to glorify Him as all creation does.
rows.anchor: افتتاح السورة بالإخبار عن تسبيح ما في السماوات والأرض لله تعالى تذكير للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening also hints that Banū al-Naḍīr suffered for arrogance toward God’s glorification: they rejected the Messenger’s truth or obstinately denied its evidence.
rows.anchor: وتعريض بأولئك الذين نزلت السورة فيهم بأنهم أصابهم ما أصابهم لتكبرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike 57:1, al-Ḥashr repeats “what” before “the earth” because this sūrah recalls an earthly favor and singles out its inhabitants; al-Ḥadīd’s opening gathers all creatures as one evidentiary whole.
rows.anchor: إلا أن التي في أول سورة الحديد فيها : { ما في السماوات والأرض وها هنا قال : ما في السماوات وما في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same opening pattern appears in al-Ṣaff, al-Jumuʿah, and al-Taghābun.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا المنوال جاءت فواتح سور الصف والجمعة والتغابن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past-tense “glorified” suits thanksgiving for the expulsion of Banū al-Naḍīr, a blessing that occurred before the sūrah was revealed.
rows.anchor: وأوثر الأخبار عن { سبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض } بفعل المضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of the expulsion may begin a new act of glorification, honoring God’s extraordinary power and implying that He should be thanked for the event.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تجعل جملة { هو الذي أخرج الذين كفروا } إلى آخرها استئنافا ابتدائيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the expulsion explains the preceding call to glorify God: it reminds Muslims and indirectly reproaches the People of the Book and hypocrites involved in the story.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تجعل علة لما تضمنه الخبر عن تسبيح ما في السماوات وما في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the expulsion explains “the Mighty, the Wise,” since this decisive subjugation manifests divine might and wisdom.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تجعل مبينة لجملة { وهو العزيز الحكيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All readings remind Muslims of God’s favor, invite gratitude, and prepare for the sūrah’s central discussion of distributing the Banū al-Naḍīr property.
rows.anchor: وعلى كل الوجوه فهو تذكير بنعمة الله على المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun and relative clause rhetorically restrict the expulsion to God, disregarding the believers’ effort and their contribution to its causes.
rows.anchor: وتعريف جزأي الجملة بالضمير والموصول يفيد قصر صفة إخراج الذين كفروا من ديارهم عليه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You did not think they would leave” functions as the rationale for the preceding rhetorical restriction of the expulsion to God.
rows.anchor: ولذلك فجملة { ما ظننتم أن يخرجوا } تتنزل منزلة التعليل لجملة القصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their belief that their fortresses would protect them supplies the reason for their confidence that they would not be expelled; the wording states the reason instead of repeating the assumed conclusion.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم يقل : وظنوا أن لا يخرجوا . مع أن الكلام على خروجهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers from the People of Scripture are Banū al-Naḍīr, a Jewish tribe settled in Arabia alongside Qurayẓah and Khaybar’s Jews; the author traces them all to Aaron.
rows.anchor: والمراد ب { الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب } بنو النضير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The placement of “Those are the truthful” parallels the placement of “Those are the successful” in al-Baqarah 2:5.
rows.anchor: وموقع قوله : { أولئك هم الصادقون } كموقع قوله : { وأولئك هم المفلحون في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most likely parsing coordinates “those who settled the abode” with “the emigrants” in the preceding verse; these settlers are the Anṣār.
rows.anchor: الأظهر أن { الذين } عطف على { المهاجرين } ( الحشر : 8 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those who settled the abode” refers to the Anṣār.
rows.anchor: والذين تبوؤا الدار هم الأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dār can mean a land or a tribe’s original territory, and can also denote a town; al-Aʿrāf 7:78 uses it for the Thamūd settlement.
rows.anchor: والدار تطلق على البلاد ، وأصلها موضع القبيلة من الأرض . وأطلقت على القرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article identifies the abode as Yathrib, and the wording presents the Anṣār as its people before describing their love for emigrants.
rows.anchor: والتعريف هنا للعهد لأن المراد بالدار : يثرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabawwuʾ means taking a place as one’s dwelling, a place to which one returns after going about one’s affairs.
rows.anchor: والتبوء : اتخاذ المباءة وهي البقعة التي يبوء إليها صاحبها

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: One exegetical reading makes the construction a metaphoric allusion that treats faith as a dwelling and “settling” as both literal and figurative.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أن يجعل الكلام استعارة مكنية بتشبيه الإيمان بالمنزل

rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes supply a verb such as “and they sincerely embraced faith,” understood from context, rather than making “faith” a direct object of “settled.”
rows.anchor: وجمهور المفسرين جعلوا المعطوف عاملا مقدرا يدل عليه الكلام

rows.speaker: الراجز الذي لا يعرف
rows.claim: The unidentified rajaz line supports supplying an omitted verb with the coordinated noun: she was fed dates and [given] cold water.
rows.anchor: نحو قول الراجز الذي لا يعرف : علفتها تبنا وماء باردا

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبعرى
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zibʿarā’s verse supports an omitted verb with the coordinated noun, “and [holding] a spear.”
rows.anchor: وقول عبد الله بن الزبعرى : يا ليت زوجكك قد غدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers parsing the waw as comitative and “faith” as an object of accompaniment, though few commentators accept this analysis.
rows.anchor: وعندي أن هذا أحسن الوجوه ، وإن قل قائلوه

rows.speaker: جمهور البصريين
rows.claim: Most grammarians treat the comitative object as attested but rare and require the verb governing it to govern its companion noun as well.
rows.anchor: والجمهور يجعلون النصب على المفعول معه سماعيا فهو عندهم قليل الاستعمال

rows.speaker: ابن هشام
rows.claim: Ibn Hishām claimed in Mughnī al-Labīb that the comitative object does not occur in the Qurʾān with certainty, interpreting 10:71 accordingly.
rows.anchor: حتى ادعى ابن هشام في ( مغني اللبيب ) أنه غير واقع في القرآن بيقين

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basrans require the verb governing an object of accompaniment to govern the noun accompanying it; the Kufans and al-Akhfash instead allow the waw to mean “with.”
rows.anchor: لأن جمهور البصريين يشترطون أن يكون العامل في المفعول معه

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash and the Kufans allow the comitative waw itself to govern, since it means “with”; ʿAbd al-Qāhir likewise says the waw governs the noun.
rows.anchor: خلافا للكوفيين والأخفش فإن الواو عندهم بمعنى ( مع )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A comitative noun need not be governed by the same verb as its companion, as shown by ordinary expressions about water and a ruler traveling with the Nile.
rows.anchor: والحق عدم التزام أن يكون المفعول معه معمولا للفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Anṣār are praised because they made the migration city their home and sheltered emigrants as a community of believers unlike any other at the time.
rows.anchor: وهو يفيد الثناء عليهم بأن دار الهجرة دارهم آووا إليها المهاجرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Before them” modifies only “settled”; the comitative waw is not coordination and functions like an adverb, so it cannot carry the preceding preposition.
rows.anchor: وبذلك يتضح أن متعلق { من قبلهم } فعل { تبوؤا } بمفرده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the city alongside faith hints at Medina’s distinction, treating their settlement there as a companion to their faith.
rows.anchor: وفي ذكر الدار ( وهي المدينة ) مع ذكر الإيمان إيماء إلى فضيلة المدينة

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Wahb reports hearing Mālik say that Medina was established through faith and migration, unlike other towns conquered by the sword; Mālik cited this verse.
rows.anchor: فيما رواه عنه ابن وهب قال : سمعت مالكا يذكر فضل المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause describing love for those who emigrated is circumstantial and praises the Anṣār’s established Islamic brotherhood, unusual among tribes receiving newcomers.
rows.anchor: وجملة { يحبون من هاجر إليهم } حال من الذين تبوؤوا الدار

rows.speaker: سعد بن الربيع
rows.claim: A report in Ṣaḥīḥ recounts Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ offering ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf half his wealth and one of his wives; the Anṣār housed emigrants and shared their palms.
rows.anchor: ما ثبت في ( الصحيح ) من خبر سعد بن الربيع مع عبد الرحمن بن عوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s pairing of emigrants and Anṣār as brothers is a sufficient illustration of the love praised here.
rows.anchor: وحسبك الأخوة التي آخى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بين المهاجرين والأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Finding” means mental perception; denying that they find a desire figuratively denies that it exists, since they would otherwise perceive it.
rows.anchor: وكنى بانتفاء وجدان الحاجة عن انتفاء وجودها لأنها لو كانت موجودة لأدركوها

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poet’s line about not seeing a lizard burrow illustrates the figurative use of perception to imply the existence of something.
rows.anchor: من باب قول الشاعر : ولا ترى الضب بها ينجحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥājah first means the need itself, then the needed object; here it figuratively means a desired aim, a common usage comparable to literal meaning.
rows.anchor: والحاجة في الأصل : اسم مصدر الحوج وهو الاحتياج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same usage means an aim in al-Muʾmin 40:80 and the purpose Jacob fulfilled in Yūsuf 12:68; al-Nābighah uses it for concealed aims.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى : { ولتبلغوا عليها حاجة في صدوركم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition “from” marks the desire as originating in the spoils granted to the emigrants.
rows.anchor: وعليه فتكون ( من ) في قوله : { مما أوتوا } ابتدائية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Their breasts” means their selves or inner life, as when “heart” denotes the inward faculties.
rows.anchor: والصدور مراد بها النفوس جمع الصدر وهو الباطن الذي فيه الحواس الباطنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What the emigrants received was the Fayʾ of Banū al-Naḍīr.
rows.anchor: و ( ما أوتوا ) هو فيء بني النضير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “their breasts” refers to the Anṣār, while the pronoun in “they were given” refers to the emigrants; the latter follows the plural sense of “who.”
rows.anchor: وضمير { صدورهم } عائد إلى { الذين تبوؤا الدار } ، وضمير { أوتوا } عائد إلى { من هاجر إليهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nearby third-person pronouns can resolve to different antecedents by context; the example from al-Rūm 30:9 and Ibn Mirdās’s poem illustrate this.
rows.anchor: مثل ( ما ) في قوله تعالى : { وعمروها أكثر مما عمروها في سورة الروم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Anṣār did not secretly aspire to take any portion of the Banū al-Naḍīr spoils given to the emigrants.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أنهم لا يخامر نفوسهم تشوف إلى أخذ شيء مما أوتيه المهاجرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ḥājah retains its literal sense of need, which can exist in the breast as an emotion; love made the Anṣār feel no lack of anything given to emigrants.
rows.anchor: ويجوز وجه آخر بأن يحمل لفظ حاجة على استعماله الحقيقي اسم مصدر الاحتياج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From what they were given” can be causal or source-marking; either reading denies felt need and its ordinary roots in rivalry and envy.
rows.anchor: وتكون ( من ) في قوله تعالى : مما أوتوا } للتعليل ، أي حاجة لأجل ما أوتيه المهاجرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted complement is “a need for anything the emigrants were given”; denying its causes also rules out its usual antecedents.
rows.anchor: وقد دل انتفاء أسباب الحاجة على متعلق حاجة المحذوف إذ التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īthār means preferring one thing over another as an act of virtue or benefit.
rows.anchor: والإيثار : ترجيح شيء على غيره بمكرمة أو منفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Anṣār deliberately preferred the emigrants, an even higher degree than lacking desire; the object is omitted because the earlier mention of what they received supplies it.
rows.anchor: وهذا أعلى درجة مما أفاده قوله : { ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا }

rows.speaker: الأنصار
rows.claim: In a report in Ṣaḥīḥ, the Prophet offered the Anṣār plots of Bahrain’s palm groves; they refused unless their emigrant brothers received equal plots.
rows.anchor: ما روي في ( الصحيح ) أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم دعا الأنصار ليقطع لهم قطائع بنخل البحرين

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Bukhārī’s report from Abū Hurayrah tells how Abū Ṭalḥah hosted a hungry visitor, putting the children to bed and extinguishing the lamp so the guest could eat their only food.
rows.anchor: فما رواه البخاري عن أبي هريرة قال : ( أتى رجل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concessive “even if” means they would prefer others despite severe need, so they surely did so under easier conditions; it does not imply impossibility.
rows.anchor: والتقدير : لو كان بهم خصاصة لآثروا على أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr compares the concessive construction with al-ʿImrān 3:91, where payment is rejected even if one offers the earth’s full weight in gold as ransom.
rows.anchor: وقد بينا ذلك عند قوله تعالى : { فلن يقبل من أحدهم ملء الأرض ذهبا ولو افتدى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaṣāṣah means severe need.
rows.anchor: والخصاصة : شدة الاحتياج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine verb is used because khaṣāṣah is not truly feminine and because a prepositional phrase separates the verb from its subject; the bāʾ denotes circumstantial association.
rows.anchor: وتذكير فعل كان } لأجل كون تأنيث الخصاصة ليس حقيقيا ، ولأنه فصل بين { كان } واسمها بالمجرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing sentence is an epilogue and parenthetical summation: protection from greed explains how they could prefer others even while needy.
rows.anchor: وجملة { ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون } تذييل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their generosity even in hardship signals freedom from avarice; whoever is spared some of its blameworthy forms succeeds to that extent.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى أن إيثارهم على أنفسهم حتى في حالة الخصاصة هو سلامة من شح الأنفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuḥḥ, with either vowel on the first consonant, is an innate impulse to withhold what belongs to oneself and is close to miserliness.
rows.anchor: والشح بضم الشين وكسرها : غريزة في النفس بمنع ما هو لها

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Ṭībī says the distinction between greed and miserliness is difficult; al-Kashshāf’s account makes miserliness an effect of greed.
rows.anchor: وقال الطيبي : الفرق بين الشح والبخل عسير جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “souls are made present with greed” in al-Nisāʾ 4:128 depicts greed as an innate trait that stays with a person.
rows.anchor: وقد قال تعالى : { وأحضرت الأنفس الشح } ( النساء : 128 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith identifies the best charity as giving while healthy and miserly, fearing poverty and hoping for wealth.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث في بيان أفضل الصدقة ( أن تصدق وأنت صحيح شحيح تخشى الفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Greed varies in degree; it is blameworthy when it leads someone to withhold good, and the blame depends on what is withheld.
rows.anchor: فإذا غلب عليها بمنع المعروف والخير فذلك مذموم

rows.speaker: الشاعر الذي لم يقف على قائله
rows.claim: An unattributed poet depicts a constricted soul resisting good deeds, illustrating the force of greed.
rows.anchor: يمارس نفسا بين جنبيه كزة إذا هم بالمعروف قالت له مهلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being protected from greed means not acquiring it as a blameworthy character; protection from all of it avoids blame, while partial protection brings proportional success.
rows.anchor: فمن وقي شح نفسه ، أي وقي من أن يكون الشح المذموم خلقا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative honors this group, and the emphatic restriction magnifies their success as though all success belonged to those protected from greed.
rows.anchor: واسم الإشارة لتعظيم هذا الصنف من الناس

rows.speaker: من المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes treat the Anṣār as a new sentence of praise and deny them any share in the Fayʾ, restricting the preceding allocation to named towns and reporting that they ceded the spoils to emigrants.
rows.anchor: ومن المفسرين من جعل { والذين تبوؤا الدار } ابتداء كلام للثناء على الأنصار

rows.speaker: منهم
rows.claim: Another group restricts this verse to the Fayʾ of Banū al-Naḍīr.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قصر هذه الآية على فيء بني النضير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects both readings as disrupting the sūrah’s coherence and relying on weak reports; he instead joins the Anṣār to the preceding group.
rows.anchor: وكل ذلك خروج عن مهيع انتظام آي هذه السورة بعضها مع بعض

rows.speaker: من المفسرين
rows.claim: On the independent-sentence reading, “they love those who emigrated to them” is the predicate of the relative subject.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا التفسير يكون عطف { والذين تبوؤا الدار } عطف جملة على جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those who came after them” is coordinated with the Anṣār under both preceding interpretations.
rows.anchor: عطف على { والذين تبوؤا الدار } ( الحشر : 9 ) على التفسيرين المتقدمين

rows.speaker: من جعلوا
rows.claim: For exegetes who coordinate the Anṣār with the poor emigrants, those who came later are a third group: people who entered Islam after both earlier groups.
rows.anchor: فأما على رأي من جعلوا { والذين تبوءوا الدار } ( الحشر : 9 ) معطوفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Coming” means entering the state of Islam, as though arriving at a place to settle; this is the third group later described as following the earlier believers in faith.
rows.anchor: والمجيء مستعمل للطرو والمصير إلى حالة تماثل حالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third group is like those described in al-Tawbah 9:100 as following the earlier believers in faith.
rows.anchor: وهؤلاء هم الذين ذكروا في قوله تعالى بعد ذكر المهاجرين والأنصار { والذين اتبعوهم بإحسان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past-tense “came” is used broadly because some Arabs and others had converted after the Hijrah; the implied sense includes those who came and those who come.
rows.anchor: وإنما صيغ { جاءوا } بصيغة الماضي تغليبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples of later converts include Ghifār, Muzaynah, Aslam, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, and Salmān al-Fārisī.
rows.anchor: مثل غفارة ، ومزينة ، وأسلم ، ومثل عبد الله بن سلام ، وسلمان الفارسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Including later Muslims prevents the misconception that only emigrants receive the Fayʾ from conquered towns, as the Prophet had allotted Banū al-Naḍīr’s spoils to them.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من هذا : زيادة دفع إيهام أن يختص المهاجرون بما أفاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse includes Muslims of every era, as ʿUmar understood when considering how Fayʾ should be distributed.
rows.anchor: وقد شملت هذه الآية كل من يوجد من المسلمين أبد الدهر ، وعلى هذا جرى فهم عمر بن الخطاب

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Al-Bukhārī transmits through Mālik from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, that ʿUmar said he would have divided every conquered town among its conquerors, as the Prophet divided Khaybar, but for later Muslims.
rows.anchor: روى البخاري من طريق مالك عن زيد بن أسلم عن أبيه قال : قال عمر

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī reports that ʿUmar consulted the emigrants and Anṣār, recited the relevant verses through “merciful,” and concluded that every Muslim was included.
rows.anchor: وذكر القرطبي : أن عمر دعا المهاجرين والأنصار واستشارهم فيما فتح الله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This interpretation concerns Fayʾ; property conquered by force is a separate legal question, including ʿUmar’s decision not to divide Iraq’s Sawād among its conquerors.
rows.anchor: وهذا ظاهر في الفيء ، وأما ما فتح عنوة فمسألة أخرى

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes who make the Anṣār passage independent also treat “those who came after them” as a new independent sentence.
rows.anchor: والفريق من المفسرين الذين جعلوا قوله تعالى
